raw: “I remember going into the wrong class at a dance studio. I had my tap shoes in a drawstring bag, and there were couples practicing a waltz around me. That was what made it sink in—everyone moving in pairs, and me standing there with the wrong shoes in a bag. I felt really out of place. I was wondering whether they’d noticed me and whether leaving would draw even more attention. It’s funny how much you can think about something as simple as walking out of a room. I look after a swimming pool for work, and I’m comfortable knowing where things belong there. This was the opposite—I was the thing that didn’t belong.”
